purpose: Where each AC-11 axis envelope comes from, so a CI lane can assemble the aggregator's manifest instead of a person assembling it by hand. tools/aggregate_ac11_evidence.py is now called by a CI lane that has run green several times, and every one of those runs recorded INVALID_RUN with the required axis envelopes absent and assembledAxes empty -- the lane exists, the envelopes do not (48-task rescore v1.11 §4-8-3), which is why its recomputed PASS count is 0/8 -- not because the axes fail, and no longer because nothing calls it, but because the per-axis lanes have not been dispatched into the same run, so there is nothing for the assembler to read. This file is the input that makes calling it possible, and it is deliberately honest about the axes that have no measurement means yet: naming them here with the reason is what keeps the aggregator's INVALID_RUN legible instead of mysterious.
note: chain is the measured state of the producer -> workflow -> importer path, read from the tree rather than asserted -- and 'the importer exists' is not the same as 'the importer emits an axis envelope', which is the mistake r1 caught. envelopeShape records what the importer actually writes: 'axis-evidence' is one envelope, 'axes-bundle' is a wrapper whose axes array holds them, and 'not-an-axis-envelope' means the importer's output cannot go into the aggregator at all. 'complete' therefore requires producer, workflow, importer AND an admissible shape. The aggregator requires all eight envelopes and refuses otherwise, so an incomplete or absent axis makes the run INVALID_RUN by design -- that is the fail-closed answer, and the reason text is what tells the reader what is in the way. importerEmitsAxes is read from the importer file as an EXACT set, not as a subset: r1 only checked that each claimed name appears somewhere, so a migration row naming one of its two axes stayed true while describing half the chain (#299 r2). A row with no importer emits nothing, so its set is empty however much its producer names. Card 216 closed the security chain: the importer now adapts the producer's report into an axis envelope (runPurpose ac11-axis-evidence, the reviewed target registry, the artifact digests it already measured), so the chain is complete in the sense this file means -- an admissible envelope exists. The axis still does not pass, for a different and narrower reason: the aggregator requires four threat reports and only SEC-SCAN-001 has a producer anywhere in this repository, so the envelope's verdict is NOT_OBSERVED and names the three that are missing. 'complete' is about the chain, not about the verdict. Measured at 097da87d with the real run 36943527856: the assembler now puts this axis into the manifest (assembledAxes names it for the first time) and the aggregator evaluates it instead of reporting it missing. r1 of that review measured what the card had left open: the aggregator refused the envelope at the common-envelope stage with 'environment.comparableGroup is required' -- INVALID_RUN, which is not an admissible envelope however complete the chain looked in this file. The aggregator requires that group on every axis envelope and the security producer does not write one, so the importer now declares this lane's group the way the accessibility and migration importers declare theirs (tools/import_ac11_accessibility_evidence.py, tools/import_ac11_migration_rehearsal.py), and only after checking that the report's environment satisfies the environment the reviewed registry requires for this target -- the name describes a set whose membership was checked rather than assumed. Re-measured at 626cbc5c with run 36949022989: the importer writes NOT_OBSERVED, the assembler names this axis in assembledAxes, and the aggregator recomputes NOT_OBSERVED for it, so the only run-level complaint left is the seven axes that are absent. The envelope also names the importer blob that wrote it and the aggregator refuses one the source tree does not contain, which is what the reviewed scan allowlist's stale pins hid: 0f614152 moved the workflow and 8933b6bd moved the importer while the pins stayed where they were, and every report copies those three pins into toolFiles, so the drift was an INVALID_RUN waiting for the three missing producers to arrive. The pins are rotated to the measured blobs and a ratchet test holds them there. The importer also stops passing a verdict through: it recomputes SEC-SCAN-001 from the payload the artifact carries and refuses to answer for the three threat reports it cannot recompute, so four rows carrying nothing but a threat ID can no longer become MEASURED_PASS. r2 measured one more thing the importer was not reading: its recomputation looked at the two counts and the four inventory lengths only, so a payload carrying a finding row nobody counted, and one whose scanners read no files and no dependencies, both recomputed MEASURED_PASS. The payload arithmetic now lives in one function in the aggregator, scan_payload_invariants, which the importer calls as well, so the two validators of 'critical and high are zero' cannot drift: the finding rows bind to the two counts, the counts to the per-scanner summaries, the summaries to the two scanner exit codes, and the coverage inventories to the files and dependencies the scanners actually read, with an empty inventory refused rather than passed. Re-measured at 3ae6b316 with run 36951113824: the axis is still NOT_OBSERVED to the aggregator, and both of the review's probes, applied to the real artifact bytes and re-signed, are refused by the invariant they break. Card 221 wired the other three threat reports. The two database ones now have a producer -- run_ac11_security_threat_reports.py measures the privileged-function catalogue and the RLS boundary against a disposable migrated database in the security lane -- and the importer carries them plus an optional SEC-VF-001 adapted from the browser lane's own proof, deciding each report's meaning with the aggregator's own evaluate_definer, evaluate_rls and evaluate_vf rather than a second opinion. Measured in the hosted lane: SEC-DEF-001 matches_reviewed_policy with fifteen functions and nothing unsafe, SEC-RLS-001 UNMEASURED because one row's identity cannot be verified for inv_cancel_bridge_owner on public.audit_events (rule E4). The axis therefore stays NOT_OBSERVED, and what is in the way is no longer code: three review decisions are. One, definerPolicySignatures lists twelve signatures while the checker's policy and the live catalogue have fifteen, and evaluate_definer's exit-0 branch requires the observed set to equal the reviewed one exactly, so SEC-DEF-001 is INVALID_RUN until the three newer privileged functions are reviewed in. Two, secVf001.workflow pins a blob of the browser lane that 0f614152 moved. That one does not show yet: evaluate_vf compares the report's toolFiles with the allowlist rather than with the tree, so SEC-VF-001 measured MEASURED_PASS from the browser lane's own proof (run 36958633624), and the aggregator only compares those pins with the source tree once all four reports are present -- measured here, adding a conforming definer report turns the axis INVALID_RUN with that single pin as the cause. The drift is latent and the two decisions have to be reviewed together -- and that pin cannot be rotated mechanically the way the dependency/SAST pins were, because the AC-11 target registry pins this same allowlist file as the target's sourceDocument, so editing it moves an AC-11 definition. Three, the unverifiable RLS row is a measurement, not a pin: closing it means either granting the identity read or reviewing the row as an accepted exception. The aggregator's RLS baseline pin was stale as well (c96f4f60 moved the file on 2026-09-28) and that one is rotated here, with a ratchet test over all four DEF/RLS pins. 2026-10-02(카드 233): security 행에 supplementalEvidence를 더했다 — 그 축의 네 report 중 SEC-VF-001은 브라우저 lane의 artifact에서 오고, 집계 lane이 그것을 importer에 넘기지 않아 lane이 만드는 봉투에서 빠져 있었다(#319 r2 측정). finder가 같은 source SHA의 run·artifact를 유일하게 찾아 문서로 적고, 검증은 importer의 vf_report 한 곳에 남는다. 못 찾으면 그 report는 조용히 빠지지 않고 봉투의 reason에 이름으로 남는다.

axes.reason: Producer and importer both exist and the importer already imports a physical run: import_report() takes the exact 22-key v1 physical report, requires both G-19 and G-24 in operatorResources, a clean tree, a window of at least 24 hours, the registered requiredEnvironment with a non-empty comparableGroup, the exact 14 case identities and fault classes, the external observer receipt, both child references, and metrics that are an exact set over the registered 48 criteria -- and from those it writes a MEASURED_PASS or MEASURED_FAIL envelope, which test_valid_physical_report_is_accepted_by_the_ac11_aggregator carries through evaluate_axis to MEASURED_PASS. What is missing is the run that would fill that report: run_ac11_composite_long_soak.py --mode physical always writes a blocked preflight report instead (G-19 without an inventory, G-24 with one) and exits 2, and no hosted runner can produce the run either (card 217, measured against the registered target s11-ac11-composite-long-soak-v0). The target requires windowSeconds >= 86400 -- 24 hours against GitHub's 6-hour job limit -- and requiredEnvironment.topology 'physical-five-node' with windowClass 'physical-24h', 5 registered / 4 eligible / 1 excluded nodes and one CP-colocated node. Several criteria cannot exist on a hosted VM at all: thermal headroom and throttle seconds, planned power-fault cases with a recovery bound, switch and WAN fault cases, and externalObserverCoveragePpm with observer 'external-monotonic-v1', which has to sit outside the measured population. faultInjection 'controlled-v1' is the G-24 adapter this repository does not own, and the producer already says so: `--mode physical` exits 2 with verdict BLOCKED_EXTERNAL, blocker G-19, 'five-node inventory is missing; no physical action was started' (measured on this PC). So a hosted workflow would be a workflow that cannot produce the evidence, and the axis definition is not lowered to fit one. The intranet execution procedure is docs/vault/40_Operations/AC-11_long-soak_사내망_실행_절차.md.
